messages:
Maya (AE): Heads-up — Cascade is live in our POC workspace behind their VPC peering. They report very slow TTFT (~2.5s baseline went to 6-8s). Also hit a security Q about KMS for model artifacts. Can ops + sec help?
Paul (AE): Customer asking how Dedicated pricing would look if we need reserved nodes due to VPC isolation. Short on time today.
Anika (SE): I can jump in. Maya — any recent config changes? model pinned, quantization?
Maya (AE): No config changes from our side. They moved traffic from hosted → private (VPC peering) yesterday afternoon.
Rani (CSM): They mentioned hitting intermittent 429s when trying to ramp concurrency during demo. Shared a snippet of their client logs: 
```
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":1.5}
```
Leo (Eng-SRE): 429s + slow TTFT usually point to batching/backpressure mismatch after network hop increases RTT. Can you grab a few request traces (x-request-id) and the runtime logs for the window after the peering cutover?
Maya (AE): Pushed their request ids to the shared GDrive. Links in thread — @Anika can you pull them?
Anika (SE): Looking at the traces — START to FIRST_TOKEN latency per request is spiking. Also seeing a lot of small batches (batch size 1-2) instead of the expected 8-16. Example from runtime log: 
```
[2026-02-20T15:42:11Z] request_id=rc-234 batch_size=1 queue_wait_ms=78 exec_ms=520 first_token_ms=620
[2026-02-20T15:42:11Z] request_id=rc-235 batch_size=12 queue_wait_ms=12 exec_ms=130 first_token_ms=142
```
Anika (SE): That suggests upstream client has inconsistent pacing after peering — more frequent small requests => batching efficiency collapse.
Tom (Security): On KMS, customer requires CMK rotation + HSM-backed wrapping for model artifacts and logs. We support KMS integration but need to confirm private deployment options. I can draft the security answers.
Leo (Eng-SRE): For immediate mitigation: 1) recommend client-side concurrency smoothing (token-bucket) to create steady request emission, 2) enable runtime batching_threshold_ms to 30ms to allow slightly longer queueing before executing, 3) confirm KV cache config — cache miss spikes would also increase exec_ms.
Rani (CSM): I'll propose a quick config experiment to the customer: enable threshold + smoothing, test for 2 hours, then share metrics. They want results before Friday demo.
Paul (AE): Pricing Q — if we move them to Dedicated due to VPC/throughput needs, what's the ballpark for a minimal commit? They asked for a 2x baseline capacity cushion.
Anika (SE): For sizing: given their peak concurrency and target latency, recommend 2 reserved GPUs (A100 equivalent) for the POC week. I'll DM numbers to you so we don't spam the thread.
Maya (AE): Thanks. Any logs showing cache miss rate? That would point to model context or KV config problem.
Anika (SE): Runtime metrics show KV cache hit rate dropped from ~92% to ~58% around the cutover window. Stack trace shows repeated cold starts on prefix keys. Possible cause: the peered network path altered sticky session / affinity to runtime instances.
Leo (Eng-SRE): Actionable checklist: 
- Confirm client is reusing HTTP keep-alive and not opening new connections per request.
- Add a short client-side batching buffer (50-100ms) to aggregate small requests where acceptable.
- On our side, bump batching_threshold_ms to 30ms and monitor p50/p95 TTFT.
- Investigate LB session affinity and the VPC peering route table for asymmetric routing.

I'll provision a debug build with extra KV cache metrics for the POC and enable verbose logging for a 1-hour window — @Maya can you get permission?
Maya (AE): I have permission, I've shared the bearer token with SRE via secure channel.
deploy-bot: Deployment started: enable-verbose-kv-metrics (deploy id: d-9876). ETA ~3m.
Anika (SE): After the small experiment (15m in) I already see avg batch size climb from 2 → 9 and FIRST_TOKEN latency drop ~45%. Still monitoring for regressions.
Tom (Security): I'll start drafting KMS questionnaire responses and include recommended network controls for VPC peering (route table validation, IAM conditionals).
Paul (AE): I'll send a short pricing snapshot for 2x reserved capacity and a note about private deployment overheads.
Rani (CSM): I'll coordinate a 30-min call with Cascade tomorrow 09:30 PT to run the config changes together and capture before/after metrics.
Maya (AE): Great — please post the deck + outcomes after the call. If throttling persists, we may need to propose a short Dedicated trial.
Anika (SE): Logging a follow-up task: SE-3589 — investigate affinity and add client keep-alive guidance to POC checklist.
Leo (Eng-SRE): I'll keep the verbose logging window open for 1 hour post-call. We should have concrete TTFT numbers to share.
Maya (AE): Thanks team :raised_hands: — feel free to DM if you hit blockers.
